citation.note: Record retention (RC 4111.08): System must retain promotion documentation (offer, effective date, wage-change justification, HR approval, equal-pay analysis if conducted) for at least 3 years to support compliance with director inspection or labor commissioner demand.

citation.section: Ohio Earned Sick and Safe Leave Act (Issue 1, effective 2025)
citation.note: Paid sick leave interaction (Issue 1, effective 2025): employees accrue 1 hour of paid leave per 30 hours worked with no cap on accrual or carryover. On promotion + pay change, if employee uses sick leave before or during promotion period, system must ensure wage upon return is not reduced below promoted rate.

body.interaction_rule: Earned sick time accrues at 1 hour per 30 hours worked with no cap on accrual or carryover. On promotion + pay change, if employee uses sick leave before or during promotion period, system must ensure wage upon return is not reduced below promoted rate; accrual continues during paid leave and does not reset on promotion.

citation.note: Pay frequency and payday change (RC 4113.15): System must flag if promotion/pay change coincides with payday change.

Final pay on separation (RC 4113.15): discharge or layoff wages due on the next regular payday or within 15 days, whichever is sooner; resignation wages due on the next regular payday. If separation follows a promotion, recalculate the final check at the promoted rate from the effective date.

body.deadline_description: Discharge or layoff: all wages due on the next regular payday or within 15 days, whichever is sooner; resignation: wages due on the next regular payday (RC 4113.15). Recalculate the final check at the promoted rate from the effective date.

citation.note: Ohio mini-WARN Act (RC 4113.31, effective September 29, 2025): 60-day advance notice to state and local officials plus employees for plant closing or layoff of 50+ employees at one site when the employer has 100+ total employees or 4,000+ combined weekly hours.

body.note: Ohio mini-WARN Act (RC 4113.31, effective September 29, 2025): 60-day advance notice to state and local officials plus employees for plant closing or layoff of 50+ employees at one site when the employer has 100+ total employees or 4,000+ combined weekly hours.

citation.note: Minimum wage $11.00/hour (2026, indexed annually per Ohio Constitution Art. II § 34a) for employers with gross receipts over $405,000; small employers pay federal minimum ($7.25).
Minimum wage $7.25/hour (federal minimum) for employers with gross receipts of $405,000 or less (Ohio Constitution Art. II § 34a).

body.worker_class: employers with gross receipts of $405,000 or less

citation.note: Equal-pay statute compliance (RC 4111.17): prohibits wage discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, or ancestry for equal work; applies to all employers with a private right of action. On promotion or pay change, flag if the new wage deviates from peer rates for equal work.

Pay-statement compliance (HB 106, RC 4113.14, effective 2025-04-09): itemized earnings and deductions stubs required each pay period, electronic or paper. On a mid-pay-period promotion, the stub issued on the next regular payday must itemize both pre- and post-promotion wages.

Whistleblower protection (RC 4113.52) applies to all Ohio employers: protects disclosure of violations reasonably believed to be criminal offenses or likely to cause imminent risk of physical harm or hazard to public health or safety, including safety-violation reports. Workers-compensation retaliation is separately barred (RC 4123.90).

No state law restricts private-sector drug testing: pre-employment, reasonable-suspicion, post-accident, and random testing are permitted per written policy. Medical marijuana (R.C. ch. 3796; R.C. 3796.28): employers need not accommodate use and may maintain drug-free workplace policies.

Data breach notification (RC 1349.19): any person or business owning or licensing computerized personal information of Ohio residents must notify affected residents within 45 days of discovering a breach of the security of the system.
